newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli court rules all beards equal in wartime.
newsitem.headline: Israeli court rules all beards equal in wartime.

text.p: Israel's Supreme Court ruled on Wednesday that bearded secular Israelis caught in a close shave with chemical warheads are entitled to the same protection as their hairy-faced religious counterparts.

The court ruled a defence ministry regulation that provided special gas masks only to Orthodox Jews, who view their beards as a religious duty, had discriminated against hirsute Israelis whose beards are for looks.

"There was discrimination against the secular man and I asked them to change it," said petitioner Akiva Nof, who shuddered at the thought of taking a razor to his chin in order to fit into a normal gas mask.

"This beard had been part of me for 20 years. I don't know myself without a beard. My wife doesn't know me without a beard. My children don't know me without a beard. This is me," Nof told reporters after winning his appeal.
During the 1991 Gulf War, Israelis donned gas masks and huddled in sealed rooms during a wave of Iraqi Scud missile attacks for fear of chemical warheads.
The special gas masks, which the defence ministry told the court cost more than twice standard ones, cover a man's beard and are designed to aid oxygen circulation.
"The court determined it is a man's right to grow a beard and the state must provide a gas mask regardless of cost," a court spokesman told Reuters.
